newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan 96/97 infrastructure to top T$450 bln-paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan 96/97 infrastructure to top T$450 bln-paper.

text.p: Taiwan's public construction projects are expected to exceed T$450 billion in value in fiscal 1996/97 (July/June), the United Daily News reported on Thursday.

The newspaper quoted the cabinet's public construction committee chairman Ou Chin-der as saying he expected the actual execution of public construction projects in 1996/97 to exceed T$450 billion, and even to reach T$500 billion at best.
Officials were not available for comment due to a holiday.
The cabinet repeatedly has pledged to speed infrastructure projects up in order to boost a slowing economy.

However, the government's crackdown on organised crime in public construction projects since mid-1996 has made government officials cautious in approving new projects, thus delaying the execution of these projects, analysts said.
Nevertheless, officials and analysts had said they expected the government's crackdown to help the construction and property sector's long-term recovery.

In fiscal 1995/96, the value of infrastructure projects was T$380 billion, compared with T$460 billion in 1994/95, T$450 billion in 1993/94 and T$390 billion in 1992/93, the paper said. -- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
